absent: Numeric values of registers, CPUID fields, correction factors, thresholds and reserved identifiers.
Internal algorithms of domain creation and teardown and generic resctrl coordination.
Full structure layouts for resources, domains, staged configuration and telemetry groups.
Error handling and concurrency beyond the shown mutex and CPU read protection.
Vendor specific memory configuration and cache allocation probing details.
Ordering guarantees for late discovery versus mount and hotplug sequencing.

findings.text: Online and offline CPU handlers maintain per resource domains and refresh per CPU reserved association while coordinating with generic resctrl bookkeeping and always indicate success.
Pre mount hook late enables package monitoring when telemetry is present by marking capability and building monitor domains for online CPUs.
Feature query reflects boot CPU support modulated by command line force markers, and event configurability is limited to bandwidth total and local when counter configuration is available.
Control plane allows writing one closid entry, applying staged values across domains, reading cached values, and querying or toggling IO allocation enablement.
Telemetry discovery reports whether any known group became usable and retains successful groups, while teardown releases retained groups; fallback builds report absence and ignore options.
Telemetry option parsing records force intent on groups matching a name with optional identity qualifier.

Late initialization prepares identifiers and vendor defaults, applies quirks, discovers allocation and monitoring, registers dynamic CPU handlers, starts generic services and announces capabilities; exit reverses telemetry, CPU handling and generic state.
CPU removal delegates to control handling when allocation is capable and to monitor handling when monitoring is capable.
Association reset returns default and current identifiers to reserved values in per CPU state and hardware.
Boot option string allows an optional leading separator and comma separated items where a leading mark means disable, with telemetry names attempted before a fixed table of cache and memory features.
A telemetry group becomes active only with usable regions, sufficient RMID capacity or explicit force, and at least one enabled event, with package RMID capacity tracking the smallest enabled group.
Telemetry regions are ignored on identity mismatch, package index outside platform limits, or MMIO length mismatch, with ignored entries made inert for later reads.
Resource discovery combines architecture presence, per feature probes, and vendor specific memory configuration to decide allocation and monitoring availability.

Level three monitor configuration derives limits, scaling, RMID population, counter width, threshold rounding, and configurable plus assignable counter support from hardware properties and sub NUMA division.
Sub NUMA handling is vendor specific, accepts only a small set of node counts, adjusts monitoring scope for clustered operation, and defaults to uniform on unexpected input.
Quirk adjustments are model selective, disabling chosen features on affected steppings, probing special allocation support, and loading a bandwidth correction factor when indexed inside its table.
Vendor defaults define cache mask sparsity and per CPU behavior plus minimum width, and select register base and update method for memory bandwidth controls including slow memory where supported.
Diagnostics use module scoped prefixes for control data and for telemetry discovery.

Domain membership changes serialize on the domain list mutex with CPU read protection for late discovery, while control application and IO toggling require CPUs held and use protected domain traversal.
Option records pair a name and feature with force markers, telemetry events pair an identifier with index and bin width, and iteration covers the known group table by bounds.

Telemetry groups rest in default, move to forced off or on by command line, become ineligible on capacity shortfall unless forced, and latch active once regions and events succeed with capacity only decreasing.
Register updates assume domain CPU membership, with single writes validated against the domain mask, batched writes executed on a domain member, and IO mode broadcast across all domains.

Association uses MSR_IA32_PQR_ASSOC with RESCTRL_RESERVED_CLOSID and RESCTRL_RESERVED_RMID defaults, IO mode toggles SDCIAE_ENABLE_BIT in MSR_IA32_L3_QOS_EXT_CFG, and bandwidth uses MSR_IA32_MBA_THRTL_BASE versus MSR_IA32_MBA_BW_BASE with MSR_IA32_SMBA_BW_BASE for slow memory.

Boot names cmt and mbmtotal and mbmlocal with l3cat and l2cat and mba and smba and bmec and abmc and sdciae plus code data variants map to matching CPU features, where a leading exclamation requests force off and plain form requests force on; telemetry names energy and perf select per RMID energy and performance features with optional hexadecimal identity qualifier.

Monitoring uses extended leaf 0x80000020 with subleaf 3 for configuration mask and subleaf 5 for counter population, a base counter width with bounded offset adjustment, and cache allocation probing uses level indexed identification.
